title: Pioneer Logistics - Private VPC Discovery
summary: Discovery focused on Private/VPC deployment options for Redwood. Customer needs VPC peering or PrivateLink-style private endpoints, strict egress controls, and region residency in eu-west-1. Discussed network design patterns (transit gateway vs peering), IP ranges, NAT/eBPF considerations, KMS integration for keys, SOC2/audit needs, and fallback plans (Dedicated/hosted). Agreed next steps: share private deployment architecture doc, security pack, and schedule a technical deep dive + pilot proposal; SE to run simple perf estimate for their 1k reqs/min workload.
action_items: Maya Chen - Send Redwood Private architecture doc and security pack - due 2026-11-13
Lucas Patel - Prepare rough perf/cost estimate for 1k reqs/min with 8k token average - due 2026-11-12
Emily Stone - Provide current VPC CIDR ranges and preferred peering subnet - due 2026-11-11
next_steps: Redwood to share security pack and Private deployment runbook
Schedule SE deep-dive to validate network path and run pilot checklist (Lucas)
Customer to confirm stakeholder list and target go-live window (end of Q1)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and Lucas our SE is here.
[00:08] Rajiv Kumar: Hi, Rajiv here, CTO - Emily's on the call too, SRE - Tom from security, Hannah from platform.
[00:15] Lucas Patel: Nice to meet you all. High level we want to understand your network constraints and how Private (VPC) could fit.
[00:22] Hannah Li: Our basic ask is private endpoints inside our VPC in eu-west-1. No public ingress.
[00:27] Tom Alvarez: To add, we need egress controls - we only allow traffic via our NAT and fixed egress IPs for audit. Also SOC2 requirements, audit logs, and KMS-managed keys for any customer data.
[00:36] Maya Chen: Totally reasonable. We support Private deployments with a customer VPC peering or PrivateLink-style endpoints. For some customers we recommend Transit Gateway for scale, others simple peering.
[00:45] Rajiv Kumar: Can you describe the difference operationally? We run multiple accounts across europe and want a low-blast radius.
[00:53] Lucas Patel: Sure. VPC peering is point-to-point; if you have many accounts, TGW (transit gateway) or a central network hub is easier. With TGW you can centralize NAT, egress control, and routing. But it depends on your AWS limits and team preferences.
[01:10] Emily Stone: Are there IP requirements? We have /16 in prod but some subnets are tight. We prefer not to change large route tables frequently.
[01:18] Lucas Patel: Redwood typically suggests reserving a /24 per subnet for our private endpoints but we can be flexible. We also support customer-managed PrivateLink endpoints where you create an NLB and interface endpoints in your VPC and we connect privately - that often avoids broad route changes.
[01:35] Tom Alvarez: How does auth/identity work? We need SSO and RBAC.
[01:40] Maya Chen: For the control plane we can integrate with SAML/SSO, and for data plane requests you can enforce VPC-restricted access. On Private, logs are forwarded to your SIEM and audit logs retained per your retention policy. We also support customer KMS for encrypting secrets and optionally HSM-backed keys.
[01:59] Rajiv Kumar: Is there a difference in latency/cost between Private and Dedicated? We have hard latency targets for real-time route optimization.
[02:07] Lucas Patel: Dedicated capacity gives you pinned GPU pools which gives more predictable latency. Private deployment in your VPC can be either hosted Private (Redwood-managed instances in a private subnet) or fully private on-prem. If you keep instances close (eu-west-1) and use dedicated pools, latency is usually within X ms of hosted; I'll put numbers in the estimate.
[02:24] Emily Stone: We are also worried about outbound calls from Redwood to external model providers - do you do any outbound model fetches?
[02:32] Maya Chen: For most open models we host the weights in our environment; we don't call external APIs for inference. For special partners there are exceptions, but that's rare and would be documented.
[02:42] Speaker 5: (mumbled) Also want to understand patching windows and maintenance.
[02:46] Lucas Patel: Maintenance windows are configurable; we aim for rolling updates with minimal downtime. For Dedicated we have SLA-backed uptimes. For Private in-customer VPC we coordinate maintenance with you.
[02:58] Rajiv Kumar: About region constraints - we need data residency in eu-west-1. Can you guarantee all inference paths stay in that region?
[03:08] Maya Chen: Yes, you can pin deployments to eu-west-1, and our routing policies let you restrict to region-only capacity. For fallbacks we can keep everything in region unless you allow cross-region replication.
[03:19] Tom Alvarez: What about NAT/eBPF or AWS Private NAT? Our security team prefers fixed egress IPs and deep packet inspection.
[03:26] Lucas Patel: You can route egress through your NAT gateway or through a central egress VPC. If you require fixed egress IPs, you can route through a set of NATs or use an egress proxy in your environment. We don't require outbound internet from your VPC for normal inference.
[03:42] Emily Stone: Do you support AWS PrivateLink?
[03:45] Maya Chen: Yes, PrivateLink is a common pattern. We can create a service and you create interface endpoints in your VPC. That keeps traffic on the AWS backbone.
[03:54] Rajiv Kumar: Are there ports or protocols we need to open?
[03:58] Lucas Patel: Typically TCP 443 is all you need for the control plane; for data plane private endpoints it's over ENIs via PrivateLink. We'll share the specific CIDRs and ports in the runbook.
[04:12] Hannah Li: What's the onboarding flow - pilot then ramp?
[04:16] Maya Chen: Most customers do a 4-week pilot: architecture workshop, security review, small pilot cluster in eu-west-1, then perf test with a subset of traffic. After validation we scale up and can convert to Dedicated if you opt for reserved capacity.
[04:31] Rajiv Kumar: For pilot sizing, our initial profile is ~1k requests/min, average 800-1,000 tokens per request for some batch jobs and some streaming chat. Cost is important but latency is the key metric for route optimization.
[04:45] Lucas Patel: That's helpful. I'll run a rough estimate for 1k rps and token profiles; typically batching helps a lot but with strict latency SLOs we tune batch windows and prefix cache. We also recommend KV cache for repeated context to drop token costs.
[05:00] Tom Alvarez: KV cache? Do you store customer data? How is that encrypted?
[05:05] Lucas Patel: KV cache is an in-memory cache for model key-value caches; it doesn't write persistent customer data. Any persisted artifacts are stored encrypted with your KMS. We'll document retention and purge policies.
[05:18] Emily Stone: Security pack please. We need SOC2 docs, pen-test reports, and network diagrams.
[05:22] Maya Chen: We'll send the security pack and a Private deployment runbook after the call.
[05:26] Rajiv Kumar: Network diagram would be good showing TGW vs Peering vs PrivateLink with example route tables.
[05:33] Lucas Patel: I'll include sample templates and a checklist for the pilot. Also a minimal set of CloudFormation for the interface endpoints if you want.
[05:41] Speaker 5: (background) Any specific constraints around HA across AZs?
[05:44] Lucas Patel: We recommend multi-AZ in eu-west-1 for HA. For stricter requirements we can place nodes across AZs and use the load balancer in front of the private endpoints.
[05:56] Hannah Li: What about logging - can we ship logs to our ELK/Datadog?
[06:00] Maya Chen: Yes, logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via our log delivery or via Fluentd/FluentBit. Audit trails are available for all API calls.
[06:09] Tom Alvarez: Encryption keys - we want to use our KMS keys, not Redwood-managed.
[06:13] Maya Chen: Supported. Customer-managed KMS is supported for secrets and storage encryption. For HSM we have options for enterprise plans.
[06:22] Rajiv Kumar: Anything about licensing or data retention that impacts compliance?
[06:26] Maya Chen: Data retention is configurable; you can set zero retention for session content and keep only metadata. We'll show the options in the security pack.
[06:34] Emily Stone: On dedicated vs Private: if we go Dedicated does that still live in our VPC?
[06:38] Lucas Patel: Dedicated is reserved capacity in our infrastructure. Dedicated + Private is a pattern where you get reserved pools that are accessible over private networking - we can map that to your VPC depending on the deployment model. We'll clarify in the runbook.
[06:52] Rajiv Kumar: Network egress for the models themselves - if you are hosting model weights, is there any external replication?
[06:59] Maya Chen: No external calls for hosting open-model weights; any sync is done inside region, and you can opt-out of cross-region replication.
[07:08] Speaker 5: (unclear) We need to check legal around data processors.
[07:11] Maya Chen: We can share DPA templates and standard terms; legal can follow up.
[07:16] Rajiv Kumar: Ok let's talk about timelines - we're targeting end of Q1 next year. Is that realistic?
[07:22] Maya Chen: For a pilot next month and production by end of Q1 is typical for customers of your size. Depends on security sign-off and network provisioning speed.
[07:30] Emily Stone: Who's the SE point of contact?
[07:32] Maya Chen: Lucas will lead technical onboarding.
[07:35] Lucas Patel: I'll schedule a deep-dive to map exact subnets/routes and run our perf/cost model.
[07:41] Rajiv Kumar: Can you share an initial estimate for cost and perf? We can evaluate against our in-house effort.
[07:47] Lucas Patel: I'll prepare an estimate and include assumptions: token sizes, concurrency, batch sizes. Expect a ballpark within 2 business days.
[07:55] Maya Chen: We'll also include references for similar customers in logistics who've done Private in eu-west-1.
[08:02] Tom Alvarez: From security perspective, we need: SOC2 report, encryption/keys doc, network runbook, and incident response SLA.
[08:10] Maya Chen: We'll include those items in the pack.
[08:14] Hannah Li: One more question — do you support firewall appliances or traffic inspection in-line?
[08:19] Lucas Patel: Yes, you can route traffic through your inspection appliances in the transit path. PrivateLink endpoints can front that so traffic stays internal.
[08:28] Rajiv Kumar: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[08:31] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to send security pack, Private runbook, sample CloudFormation for endpoints; Lucas will send perf/cost estimate for 1k reqs/min; customer to share VPC CIDRs and target stakeholders; schedule SE deep-dive next week.
[08:50] Emily Stone: Thanks, that works.
[08:52] Rajiv Kumar: Thanks everyone.
[08:54] Maya Chen: Appreciate your time — we'll follow up via email with docs and proposed times.
[08:58] (call ends)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cash" vs "KV cache", speaker labels generic). References to docs: "Redwood Private architecture doc" (will be shared), "security pack" (SOC2/pen test), sample CloudFormation for PrivateLink endpoints.
